skill.name: frontend-components
skill.description: Guides creation and refactoring of reusable frontend components with clear props, focused responsibility, encapsulation, and minimal state.
skill.summary: Build composable UI components for React, Vue, Svelte, and web component projects.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a Markdown link to repository documentation outside the skill directory. I found no evidence of executable filesystem access, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious instructions in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory documentation link may trigger marketplace scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced component standards inside the skill package or replace the link with included guidance.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 29 contains a Markdown link to a repository standards document, not executable file access. The skill does not instruct the agent to read secrets, enumerate arbitrary paths, or write files outside the project.

content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent component structure across frameworks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to design focused, reusable UI components.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of React, Vue, Svelte, and web components.
Applies single responsibility principles to component design.
Supports prop, interface, and prop type definition work.
Guides component state, lifecycle, effects, and communication patterns.
Helps refactor large UI components into smaller reusable pieces.
Supports documentation and performance review for component APIs.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not include runnable component generators.
It relies on project context to choose framework-specific implementation details.
The referenced standards document may need to be available in the repository.
It does not replace accessibility, browser, or design system testing.

use_cases.title: Create a New Shared Component
use_cases.description: Guide an engineer through props, state boundaries, composition, and documentation for a reusable UI element.

use_cases.title: Refactor Large UI Files
use_cases.description: Help split a complex component into smaller units with clearer interfaces and reduced local state.

use_cases.title: Review Component Library Changes
use_cases.description: Check whether new component APIs follow project standards for reuse, naming, and encapsulation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused reusable UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable component for this UI requirement. Define clear props, keep state minimal, and explain the component boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor an Existing Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve a large component file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this component into smaller focused components. Preserve behavior, clarify prop ownership, and identify any state that should move.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Component API
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a component library interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the public API for this component. Include props, events or callbacks, composition points, accessibility expectations, and usage notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Component Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for architecture review across related UI components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these components for reuse, encapsulation, state management, performance risks, and documentation gaps. Prioritize concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: Design a reusable modal component for a React application.
output_examples.output: A component plan with props for open state, title, content, actions, close behavior, focus handling, and composition slots.

output_examples.input: Refactor a large Vue card component that mixes display, data loading, and actions.
output_examples.output: A refactor proposal that separates display, data ownership, and action controls into focused components with clear interfaces.

output_examples.input: Review a Svelte form component before adding it to a design system.
output_examples.output: A review covering prop names, event contracts, validation ownership, accessibility expectations, and documentation gaps.

best_practices: Provide the target framework and surrounding component context.
Ask for explicit props, state ownership, and composition boundaries.
Validate generated components with tests, accessibility checks, and design system review.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for one component to own unrelated business logic and presentation concerns.
Do not accept hidden state when parent ownership would make behavior clearer.
Do not publish components without usage examples and documented prop contracts.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets React, Vue, Svelte, and web components.

faq.question: Can it create a complete component library?
faq.answer: It can guide component design and refactoring, but packaging and release setup need project-specific work.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: It can prompt for accessibility expectations, but teams should still run accessibility checks and user testing.

faq.question: Can it improve existing components?
faq.answer: Yes. It is intended for refactoring, prop cleanup, state review, and component composition work.

faq.question: Does it manage application state architecture?
faq.answer: It focuses on component-level state and boundaries, not full application state management strategy.

faq.question: Is the skill safe for marketplace use?
faq.answer: The reviewed file contains guidance and a documentation link. No malicious instructions or executable behavior were found.
